name: Swara Baby Products
summary: Swara Baby Products, promoted by FirstCry parent Brainbees Solutions, is the largest contract manufacturer of disposable hygiene products such as baby and adult diapers in India, with four plants in Madhya Pradesh. Revenue grew from ₹767 cr in FY24 to ₹1,212 cr in FY26 and profit rose 18.5% in FY26 to ₹95.6 cr, but the net margin fell from about 12% to about 8% and borrowings grew faster than revenue to ₹443 cr. At ₹111 the post-issue market cap is ₹3,211.56 cr, about 33.6 times FY26 profit and 3.05 times post-issue book value, and the RHP names no listed peers to compare against. The top 10 customers give 80.3% of revenue and sales to related parties (mainly Brainbees) are about 25.7% of revenue, shares were allotted and transferred at an adjusted ₹22.50 within the last year, and cases are pending against the promoters and a director.

fh1.finding: Revenue rose from ₹766.6 cr (FY24) to ₹1,212.4 cr (FY26), a CAGR of about 25.8%.

fh2.finding: Revenue grew every year: ₹766.6 cr, ₹959.7 cr, ₹1,212.4 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh3.finding: Debt to equity was 0.81 at 31 March 2026.

fh4.finding: Borrowings rose 70% (₹260.1 cr to ₹443.1 cr) while revenue rose 58% over FY24–FY26.

fh5.finding: Net worth rose every year: ₹319.4 cr, ₹399.9 cr, ₹553.2 cr (FY24–FY26).

fh6.finding: FY26 operating cash flow was ₹74.87 cr, about 78% of PAT of ₹95.59 cr.

pr1.finding: Profit after tax rose about 18.5% in FY26, to ₹95.6 cr from ₹80.7 cr.

pr2.finding: Net margin fell from about 12.3% in FY24 (PAT ₹94.0 cr on ₹766.6 cr) to 8.2% in FY26.

pr3.finding: Return on net worth was 17.28% in FY26 (ROE 20.06%).

pr5.finding: The RHP says there are no listed peers of comparable size, scale and business model.

va1.finding: No listed peers are named in the RHP, so P/E cannot be compared; post-issue P/E at ₹111 is about 33.6x FY26 PAT.

va2.finding: No listed peers are named in the RHP, so P/B cannot be compared; post-issue P/B at ₹111 is about 3.05x.

va3.finding: No listed peers are named in the RHP, so market cap to sales cannot be compared; it is about 2.76x FY26 revenue from operations.

va4.finding: Shares were allotted in December 2025 and transferred in March 2026 at an adjusted ₹22.50, about 80% below the ₹111 upper band.

pg1.finding: Promoter and promoter group holding falls from 100% to 75.09% after the issue.

pg2.finding: The RHP states promoter shares are not pledged or encumbered, apart from a 1.62% non-disposal undertaking.

pg3.finding: FY26 sales to related parties were ₹299.5 cr, about 25.7% of revenue from operations, with Brainbees alone at 22.64%.

pg4.finding: Pending against promoters: 2 criminal, 3 regulatory and 16 tax cases (₹16.68 cr), plus criminal cases against director Supam Maheshwari.

is1.finding: The offer for sale is ₹300 cr of the ₹799.88 cr issue, about 37.5%.

is2.finding: The ₹799.88 cr issue is about 24.9% of the ₹3,211.56 cr post-issue market cap at ₹111.

is3.finding: Selling shareholders sell equal amounts at costs of ₹24.55 (Brainbees) and ₹2.13 (Anadya), an average of ₹13.34, so ₹111 is about 8.3x their cost.

up1.finding: ₹198.21 cr of the ₹499.88 cr fresh issue (about 39.7%, just under the line) is for capex on a new project.

up2.finding: ₹127.5 cr (about 25.5%) of the fresh issue repays borrowings of the company and its subsidiaries.

up3.finding: The general corporate purposes amount is not fixed; the RHP caps it at 25% of the fresh issue.

up4.finding: All loans to be repaid are from HDFC Bank, and the RHP says the Brainbees loan will not be repaid from the proceeds.

lg1.finding: Cases against the company and subsidiaries total about ₹3.39 cr, about 0.6% of ₹553.22 cr net worth.

lg2.finding: No criminal or regulatory cases against the company, but promoter Brainbees faces customs (₹6.57 cr) and other cases and a director faces criminal cases.

lg3.finding: Contingent liabilities were ₹0.14 cr at 30 June 2026, 0.03% of net worth.

rk1.finding: The top 10 customers gave 80.31% of FY26 revenue from operations, with Brainbees at 22.64%.

rk2.finding: The top 10 suppliers were 69.43% of FY26 purchases; the largest single supplier share was not found.

rk3.finding: The company was incorporated in November 2016, about 10 years ago.

rk4.finding: The statutory auditor, Walker Chandiok & Co LLP, gave unmodified opinions on the restated financials.
